chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Sa'dan, from Abu Mas'ud, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Good neighbourliness increases the lifespan, and building the households.'

key_terms.حُسْنُ الْجِوَارِ: Good neighbourliness / excellence in maintaining neighbourly relations

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual and physical benefits of good neighbourliness according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links the ethical practice of good neighborliness (husn al-jiwar) directly to the prolongation of life (ziyadah fi al-a'mar), a concept often interpreted by Shia scholars as both literal physical longevity and spiritual vitality. The mention of 'imarat al-diwar' (building/maintaining dwellings) underscores the importance of domestic stability and material care as foundational elements of a righteous household, reinforcing the hadith's emphasis on the interplay between social ethics and personal well-being.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from his father, from Sa’dan, from Abu Masoud who said,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘The good neighbourliness increases in the life-span and the building of the households’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar ibn ‘Abd al-‘Aziz from Zurara from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“Once Fatimah (a.s.) came to the Messenger of Allah and complained about certain matters. The Messenger of Allah gave her a tablet to read. It was written on the tablet: ‘Whoever believes in Allah and the Day of Judgment must not cause suffering to his neighbor. Whoever believes in Allah and the Day of Judgment must treat his guest with honor. Whoever believes in Allah and the Day of Judgment must speak of good or remain silent.’”
